runs.name: Oil States International, Inc.; NYSE OIS, manufactured products and services for the energy, military and industrial sectors in three segments, Offshore Manufactured Products, Completion and Production Services and Downhole Technologies; no rename, merger, spin-off or split in the 8-Ks since 2025-01; auditor changed from EY to Deloitte 2025-02-27; a cash flow credit agreement 2026-01-28; Cindy B. Taylor retired as CEO 2026-05-01, Lloyd A. Hajdik her successor; NOV, Baker Hughes and Tenaris read as the first three filing rivals the 10-K names, Hutchinson and OneSubsea flagged
runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$7.94** (2026-10-15 close, through `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged). Shares **60,322,619** (10-Q cover, 0001121484-26-000033, `Screens/cover_shares.py`; checked against 82,179,784 issued less 21,836,542 treasury at 2026-06-30; the 529,428 shares of 2026-04-01 that retired the 2026 notes inside the count); cap **$479M**; debt on face $18M at 2026-06-30, net debt about $0.8M (the borrowings reported 2026-07-28 left out, the cash that day not stated). Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury par curve, 30-year, 2026-10-15). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (0001121484-26-000007), the 10-Q to 2026-06-30, the proxy (0001121484-26-000017), the 2025 and 2026 8-Ks, the segment notes of the FY2015, FY2017, FY2019, FY2022 and FY2023 10-Ks; one figure cross-checked (2025 operating cash $105,123K, filed statement against XBRL). Lines of evidence and rivals derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7 (the brief's departure), stated in the run file. Balance sheets 2014 to 2025 read in Step 0: equity $1,341M to $573M, written off rather than paid out (buybacks about $55M 2017 to 2025); goodwill to $647M with the 2018 GEODynamics and Falcon purchases, then impaired $165.0M 2019, $406.1M 2020, $10.0M 2024, and $121.1M of impairments in 2025; receivables 23% to 30% of sales and inventory 22% to 27% 2019 to 2025; debt $274M to $18M. Q1 IN (a cyclical supplier of engineered oilfield equipment, oil-price dependence not a STOP by itself). **Q2 OUT**: a standing castle that protects only ordinary returns over the full cycle. Offshore Manufactured Products decides, carrying more than all of the segments' combined operating profit 2021 to 2025 ($251.5M against -$34.9M and -$171.3M for the land segments); it earned about 12% pre-tax on its assets less goodwill 2014 to 2025 before corporate costs and about 8% after a revenue share of them (the allocation a CONVENTION of the run), low single digits 2017 to 2022, high only at the 2014 to 2016 and 2023 to 2025 peaks; the company lost money at the operating line in 8 of 11 years 2015 to 2025; the filer's own risk factors: "relatively few barriers to entry", contracts "awarded on a bid basis"; average operating income on assets NOV -2.9% (0.8% with impairments added back) 2014 to 2025, Baker Hughes -1.8% (1.7%) 2014 to 2024, Tenaris 8.5% 2016 to 2025, Oil States -4.3% (-0.6%) 2014 to 2025; Hutchinson and OneSubsea flagged as non-filers; the 10-K names no rival for the two land segments. Q3 to Q12 not reached. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged:** impairments in six of the seven years 2019 to 2025; the Q2 2026 release leads with Adjusted EBITDA and pay is set on an EBITDA target; a $1.65M cash bonus to the former CEO for 2025, a year with a $109M net loss; the new CEO's change-of-control severance amended 2026-07-09 to 3.0 times salary plus target bonus; the auditor changed from EY to Deloitte in 2025 with no disagreements. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: owner cash all spending deducted $14.5M a year 2021 to 2025, $37.6M a year over the 2017 to 2021 organic cycle; the one 2018 purchase triggers the serial-acquirer convention, applied as written, organic pair central; value **$5.95 to $13.69** a share all-equity against $7.94 (bottom a 10.7% yearly decline, top no growth), no case earning the floor, best 9.4% with a $36.8M 2020 tax refund in its base; fair price **$5.58 all-equity** ($4.68 equity-only beside); not armed, the box being OUT at Q2. Contamination declared by the analyst: the USAC fold commit subjects and research-folder names in its opening context, a `Test Runs/` directory listing of 2026-10-1x file names (other companies only, no OIS file), memory-index lines about the queue; none used, the USAC subject named as the one that could have anchored the run. Commits b8088ab5, 4056a2c0, f3596f13, b2caa809, four. Position note filled at the fold: not held (`PORTFOLIO.md` carries no line for OIS or Oil States). Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` PASS (29 ids); the dispatcher's `dispatcher_cite_check.py` no missing id, no E-id and no slip among 21 tight pairs; the wider sweep's misses are filing quotations, the framework's own wording and quote-boundary artifacts, none beside a ledger row's words. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) whether a part's ordinary returns are read before or after the costs kept at the centre (here about 12% against about 8%); (2) which series defines the full cycle at Q2 (revenue, operating income, owner cash), owner cash here running against the cycle; (3) the serial-acquirer convention triggered by one large purchase in the window, which is not what "serial" describes; (4) what stands in for a named rival where the filer names none, here for the two land segments. Could not get: Baker Hughes's 2025 and Tenaris's pre-2016 operating income untagged; the rivals' figures transcribed from tagged data, not checked against their statements; the offshore segment redefined in 2017 and 2024; no maintenance capital disclosed.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT: a castle that stands but protects only ordinary returns over the full cycle: the deciding offshore segment about 12% pre-tax on assets less goodwill 2014 to 2025 before corporate costs and about 8% after, low single digits 2017 to 2022, high only at the peaks; the company lost money at the operating line in 8 of 11 years; the filer's own words, relatively few barriers to entry and bid-basis contracts; the named rivals NOV, Baker Hughes and Tenaris ordinary or less; the 2018 GEODynamics purchase written down through four rounds of impairment. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: Adjusted EBITDA featured and pay on an EBITDA target, a cash bonus in a loss year, an amended change-of-control severance, an auditor change without disagreements. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: value $5.95 to $13.69 a share all-equity against $7.94, fair $5.58 all-equity ($4.68 equity-only), not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: segment returns before or after central costs; which series defines the cycle; the serial-acquirer convention on one deal; rivals where the filer names none.
